shared_infrastructure_notes: All three tasks share ONE Week2LLMGateway instance per run, and therefore ONE timeout value and ONE retry count -- there is currently no per-task override plumbed into invoke_json_with_trace (the per-call override parameters timeout_seconds/max_retries exist only on the separate invoke_prebuilt_json_prompt method, used exclusively by the Phase 1B.1 Shadow evaluation path, never by the three production tasks).

call_with_timeout() creates a FRESH single-worker ThreadPoolExecutor for EVERY attempt and calls future.cancel() on timeout -- since ThreadPoolExecutor cannot forcibly interrupt a running thread, a timed-out call's underlying model invocation may continue running in the background after the caller moves on; any late response is simply discarded, never observed or logged. This means the log record NEVER reveals how long an orphaned call's true completion would have taken.
The retry loop reuses the IDENTICAL prompt string on every attempt -- no input truncation, no prompt modification, no request-shape change between attempts.

provider_attempts/retry_count in llm_semantic_calls.jsonl is per LOGICAL call across all its attempts; the persisted 'latency_ms' field for a call that succeeded on a retry is the TOTAL wall-clock duration across ALL prior failed attempts plus the successful one -- NOT the successful attempt's own duration alone. This was empirically confirmed (e.g. a TSM_OLD alpha_classifier retried-success shows latency_ms=76136, i.e. ~45000ms consumed by the failed first attempt's timeout plus ~31000ms for the successful second attempt).

error_taxonomy.note: SCHEMA_EXHAUSTED corresponds to WEEK2_LLM_VALIDATION_FAILED as terminal cause (structure_extractor's dominant failure mode); no PARSE_EXHAUSTED (WEEK2_LLM_INVALID_JSON) or RATE_LIMIT_EXHAUSTED (WEEK2_LLM_RATE_LIMIT) ever appeared as a TERMINAL (attempt-2) cause in any of the 6 original runs, though both codes exist in the taxonomy and appear as non-terminal attempt-1 events in small numbers.

alpha_classifier.reasoning: Prompts are small (~1800-1850 chars mean), successful calls typically complete in low single-digit seconds; retried-success latencies are mostly 1-6s for the second attempt, with only 2 of many recovered calls (TSM_OLD) taking a second attempt close to the 45s ceiling. High recovery rate (72%) is consistent with transient blips, not systematic under-provisioning.

evidence_stance_classifier.reasoning: Terminal cause is 100% WEEK2_LLM_TIMEOUT in 5 of 6 runs (AMD's cluster is the transport-error exception). Retried-successes' TOTAL latency (first failed 45s attempt + second attempt) frequently lands at 76-90 SECONDS across MSFT/SNDK/TSM_OLD, meaning the second attempt alone often consumes 31-45 seconds -- right up against the SAME 45s ceiling it just cleared. This component's typical successful latency profile runs close enough to the current timeout that a nontrivial fraction of attempts land on the losing side of the boundary purely by chance, which is consistent with (though not proof of) the observed near-zero (2.66%) recovery rate.

structure_extractor.reasoning: Terminal cause is dominated by WEEK2_LLM_VALIDATION_FAILED (schema/parse), not timeout, in 5 of 6 runs. Timeout is not the binding constraint for this component's final orphans.

timeout_root_cause_audit.overall_answer: UNCERTAIN -- YES specifically and only for evidence_stance_classifier; NO for alpha_classifier; NOT_APPLICABLE for structure_extractor. This audit does not recommend a blanket timeout increase.

transport_error_audit.clustering: ALL 67 events share the identical logged timestamp 2026-09-07T00:09:51Z, spanning attempt=1 (33) and attempt=2 (34), across evidence_stance_classifier (58) and structure_extractor (10 events, wait 57+10=67 -- evidence_stance=57 raw total per earlier count, 58 total-including-1-timeout-at-that-instant)
transport_error_audit.retry_behavior: Of calls whose FIRST attempt hit this transport-error window, essentially none recovered on the second attempt (evidence_stance_classifier's overall AMD recovery rate is 0%) -- consistent with an outage that was still in effect (or had just ended without a delay to let it clear) when the immediate, no-backoff retry fired.
transport_error_audit.final_orphans_disproportionately_transpo: YES for AMD specifically (29 of evidence_stance_classifier's 33 AMD final orphans are TRANSPORT_ERROR-terminal, vs TIMEOUT-terminal in every other run) -- AMD is a genuine outlier, not representative of the other 5 runs.
transport_error_audit.transient_vs_deterministic: TRANSIENT -- the single-instant clustering strongly indicates a brief, shared network/connection-layer disruption (e.g. a dropped connection pool or DNS blip) rather than a per-request deterministic defect. A short backoff delay before retry (not implemented, not proposed as active in this task) would plausibly have let such a brief outage clear before the retry fired -- but this is inference from the clustering pattern, not directly measured.
transport_error_audit.connection_reuse_note: Not directly inspectable from these logs -- the LLM client's internal connection/session handling is inside tradingagents.llm_clients.create_llm_client, not modified or executed in this task.

tsm_old_vs_new_reliability_control.what_changed_operationally: Nothing in configuration. Both runs used the same .env-configured timeout (45s) and retry count (1), the same model/provider, the same concurrency setting, and produced near-identical alpha_classifier recovery rates (76.3% old vs 77.8% new) and orphan rates (23.7% old vs 22.2% new) -- statistically indistinguishable given the small sample sizes involved. The specific A301-carrying claim happened to land in the ~22-24% tail that exhausts both attempts in the old run, and in the ~76-78% majority that recovers (or in this case succeeds outright) in the new run. This is the expected behavior of a probabilistic retry-exhaustion process operating on two DIFFERENT claim instances (different research content -> different claim_id) carrying the SAME underlying economic thesis and deterministic strength.

For alpha_classifier, this option would mean giving Pure-LLM Semantic Authority a deterministic fallback it deliberately does not have today.
files_functions_likely_touched: alpha_mapper.py -- would require introducing a NEW fallback path where none exists by design
option_d_deterministic_fallback_preserva.semantic_behavior_changed: YES for the alpha_classifier variant -- this is a SEMANTIC AUTHORITY change (Pure-LLM Semantic Authority currently has no intermediate fallback BY DESIGN), not a reliability-only change. Per task section 24, this belongs to a different semantic-design task, not this reliability-only audit.
option_d_deterministic_fallback_preserva.tsm_a301_benefit: Would have masked, not fixed, the OLD run's A301 miss by substituting a non-LLM decision -- explicitly NOT recommended per task section 24's warning against using TSM A301's deterministic eligibility to justify a global bypass of Pure-LLM Semantic Authority
option_d_deterministic_fallback_preserva.implementation_readiness: OUT_OF_SCOPE for alpha_classifier (semantic-design task); ALREADY_EXISTS for evidence_stance_classifier/structure_extractor (no action needed)

option_e_concurrency_rate_smoothing.summary: Reduce/smooth concurrency to avoid Provider-side rate limiting or contention
option_e_concurrency_rate_smoothing.root_cause_addressed: NONE -- concurrency_audit found no evidence concurrency causes failures; if anything the only concurrent component (alpha_classifier) performs best
option_e_concurrency_rate_smoothing.implementation_readiness: DESIGN_NOT_READY -- not supported by evidence, not recommended

option_f_transport_retry_hardening.summary: Add a short backoff delay before retry specifically for TRANSPORT_ERROR-classified attempts (not a blanket backoff for all error types)
option_f_transport_retry_hardening.root_cause_addressed: AMD's 67-event single-instant TRANSPORT_ERROR cluster -- a brief shared-infrastructure outage that an immediate, no-delay retry could not outlast
files_functions_likely_touched: week2_llm.py's retry loop -- would need a conditional short sleep only in the TRANSPORT_ERROR/RATE_LIMIT branch
option_f_transport_retry_hardening.expected_final_orphan_effect: Plausible reduction in AMD-pattern transport clusters specifically (13.8% of all final orphans, concentrated in AMD)
option_f_transport_retry_hardening.provider_behavior_changed: YES -- adds a delay between attempts for transport-classified failures only
option_f_transport_retry_hardening.regression_risk: LOW-MEDIUM -- adds wall-clock time only on an already-failing path; needs care to keep the delay short and bounded
option_f_transport_retry_hardening.tsm_a301_benefit: NONE (A301's old miss was TIMEOUT, not transport)
option_f_transport_retry_hardening.amd_transport_benefit: DIRECT -- this is the AMD-specific fix
option_f_transport_retry_hardening.blast_radius: Narrow -- only fires on TRANSPORT_ERROR/RATE_LIMIT classified attempts, all components
option_f_transport_retry_hardening.implementation_readiness: DESIGN_NOT_READY (not this task) -- but well-supported by evidence as a SECONDARY, lower-priority future candidate given its narrower scope (13.8% of orphans, effectively one run's worth of evidence) vs Option C's 74%

preferred_reliability_fix.chosen_option: OPTION_C -- component-specific retry-count increase for evidence_stance_classifier only
preferred_reliability_fix.not_chosen_based_on_alpha_hit_gain: Correct -- evidence_stance_classifier's Gold-alpha impact is currently UNKNOWN (no attribution tool exists, per gold_impact section). This fix is chosen purely because it addresses the dominant (74%) source of final-orphan volume with the best-supported, lowest-risk mechanism, not because it is expected to move the 61.0317% Alpha Hit number in any particular direction.

tsm_a301_historical_fixture_unaffected -- confirm this change does not alter alpha_classifier's retry count or A301's already-established outcome in either historical TSM run (regression fixture, replayed offline)

future_validation_ticker.reasoning: TSM has BOTH a proven alpha_classifier reliability-sensitive lineage (A301, already the canonical positive control) AND meaningful evidence_stance_classifier orphan volume (30 old-run / 32 new-run final orphans) to observe the preferred fix's effect on directly. Selected from evidence, not merely because TSM was mentioned first in the task.

preferred_metrics: evidence_stance_classifier final-orphan rate decreases (from the current 97.34% orphan-rate-given-failure)
evidence_stance_classifier final_orphans count decreases run-over-run for the same ticker profile
claims_orphaned_by_provider_failure (currently alpha_classifier-scoped) remains unaffected or improves, never worsens
impacted Gold Alphas do not increase
no semantic regression (P0/P1, B1/B2/B4, activation formulas all byte-identical in behavior)
success_criteria_for_future_fix.tsm_specific_control: A301 remains NOT Provider-impacted (i.e. this evidence_stance-scoped fix must not touch alpha_classifier's independent A301 lineage) -- an important negative control to check post-fix.

should_provider_reliability_block_msft_a.reasoning: MSFT A304 was independently confirmed NOT Provider-caused in the prior Phase 2 recall recovery audit -- MSFT's own impacted_alpha_ids is [A301], not [A304], and A301 is already a Gold hit for MSFT (IMPACTED_BUT_REDUNDANT, confirmed again in this audit's Section 19 table). There is no causal or resourcing dependency between the evidence_stance_classifier reliability fix proposed here and MSFT A304's own blocker (a regex/negation-aware extraction capability gap, per the prior audit).

development_plan_recommendation.label: Implement bounded Provider reliability fix next (Option C, evidence_stance_classifier retry increase), then validate on TSM, then proceed to MSFT A304
development_plan_recommendation.reasoning: The preferred fix is READY_FOR_BOUNDED_IMPLEMENTATION, well-evidenced, low-risk, and offline-testable. It does not block or depend on MSFT A304 work (confirmed NO above), so the two tracks could in principle run in parallel -- but per the task's sequential framing, PLAN_A (fix, then TSM validation, then MSFT A304) is recommended as the cleaner, one-track-at-a-time execution order, not because MSFT A304 requires waiting.
